title: The Shapeshifter
subtitle: What you learn in school isn't always useless—run into enough trouble, and you'll find a moment to put it to use.

items.text: The Shapeshifter
Book Stacks, Library

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Excuse me, miss. May I borrow this book?

items.speaker: School Librarian
items.text: Five Easy Recipes to Brew an Invisibility Potion? Are you sure you've picked the right book, dear? The final exams are coming up, and I doubt this appears anywhere on your syllabus.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No, it doesn't, but ...
She hunches her shoulders.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I just want something different to read. I've gone through every book on the syllabus, or at least stared at them until my brain gave up.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll probably fail. Maybe that's for the best.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Merel!
A noise from the nearby bookshelves grabs Merel's attention. She turns to see another girl approaching her, beaming with confidence.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: S-Sorry. Do I know you?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I am Matilda Bouanich. Though you have doubtlessly heard of me.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Um, okay. How did you know my name?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Why, I remembered it, of course. I remember everyone's name. You should learn to do the same, starting with mine. That way, you'll know who to turn to if you need any help.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: You're one of the new students, isn't that right?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Yeah.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I know you've been struggling, but not everyone arrives having mastered the entire syllabus as I have. You'll get the hang of it in no time. Trust me.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I guess so. Are you borrowing books too? What did you get? An Introduction to Shapeshifting and Its Practice Through Time?
An intimidating book, thick as a brick. Merel doesn't need to open it to know every page will be filled with walls of teeny-tiny text.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Are you trying to learn to shapeshift, Matilda?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I just want to get a taste of it, that's all.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But that book's huge. Err, how about Fiddler Crab Shapeshifting for Dummies? I've read it. It's simple and fun, perfect for beginners like us.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Excuse me?! I've never read a more insulting title! Matilda Bouanich is no "dummy," and she absolutely will not read a book that is meant for one!

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: If I am to learn shapeshifting, I will do it properly and learn from the best! I will not end up as some sorry, soggy, crabby little thing crawling around on the floor.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Besides, we've already had quite enough dummies knocking on the infirmary's door with claws instead of hands.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Though, I did hear Sonetto once borrowed that book. But I simply cannot imagine her turning into a crab. Hmm. I wonder if she succeeded? There must be a way I can find out.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: N-Nevermind. Why would Matilda concern herself with such petty tricks? We Bouaniches have already mastered something far more powerful—command of the crystal orbs.
Matilda walks away, hefting a copy of An Introduction to Shapeshifting and Its Practice Through Time.
Reading Room, Library
She holds a book she picked up from the library corridor.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: To be honest, I wasn't exactly thrilled when they told me I'd be sent here. But I guess there are worse places I could've been stationed, so I didn't complain.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I can't say I've missed the school announcements, or the electric fences and detention rooms. Not even for a second.
She places the book beside Matilda's pillow.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But I've always liked the library. It's probably the only part of this school that I did.
She's alive but hasn't stirred at all since they brought her in.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I will see this through, Matilda. Not for the sake of the school, though—

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: The instructors are hiding something. But if we'll find out one day anyway, why don't they just tell us now?

items.speaker: Emilia
items.text: Miss, why can't you just tell us what's happening out there? I swear we'll keep our mouths shut.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: Don't bother, Emilia. They're not gonna tell you anything.

items.speaker: Lucas
items.text: They know. But even if they used to be students like us, they're just like them now.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: —But for our friends and for the students who remind me of who we once were.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: This war will end someday. And when it does, I hope they'll live in a kinder world than the one we grew up in.
Merel, hearing light footsteps echo behind her, turns around.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Merel, is Ms. Bouanich going to be okay?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: *sigh* She still hasn't regained consciousness. It might have something to do with the arcane skill that hit her.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But her vitals are stable, and the casualty assessment didn't show anything serious. The rehab center should have her back on her feet in no time.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Casualty assessment?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Yeah. It's a process I learned back at the Vigiles Bureau. Just glad I haven't forgotten it.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: The Vigiles Bureau ... Was that your first job after school? You're incredible.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I doubt my instructor back then would agree. I didn't do very well in the exams.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Ms. Bouanich once told me that grades aren't everything. You must have had other strengths the Vigiles Bureau valued.
Lavender's reverent gaze makes it hard for Merel to tell her the truth.
How could she confess that her grades were so bad that nobody except Creius, who was so desperate he'd accept any graduate with a pulse, would take her in?

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: When I graduate, I hope I can join the Vigiles like you or be an investigator, like Ms. Bouanich. Do you think I stand a chance?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Of course! But you should really consider working at the Foundation's headquarters. It's much safer behind a desk than out in the field.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I don't want to be stuck indoors. Besides ...

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Ms. Bouanich and Ms. Sonetto chose to be field operatives, and so did you. You all must've seen a reason to do it.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I don't really know all the details of what investigators, Vigil officers, or soldiers actually do out there, but I know it's what I want to do.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: They aren't all that different, really. Sometimes you'll find their duties overlap.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Merel?
Sonetto stands in the reading room's doorway.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Over here! Matilda's condition hasn't changed. Is there something you need?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The Timekeeper wants a word with you in the study room.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Sure. I'm on my way.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: I better go check on the other students again—see how they've been behaving.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Some of the younger ones think they might find a solution to the impending "Storm" in the books. But I figure if the answer really was in a book, someone would have found it already.
Lavender exits the room and reenters the crowd of nervous students in the library corridor.
Study Room, Library
Despite the mess, the study room's atmosphere feels solemn. Merel can't help but sense the tension.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: You wanted to see me? What's wrong?
She looks away from the window.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The convoy should've arrived by now, but there's no sign of them. I haven't been able to reach headquarters either.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm afraid we have to prepare for the worst.
Merel approaches the table, looking over the map that they've laid out depicting the SPDM campus.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Is this the contraction rate of the immunity area?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. Its radius has reduced by 30 meters in the last 15 minutes. It's shrinking even faster than I'd anticipated.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At this rate, the library will be exposed ten minutes before the "Storm" arrives.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But, there are so many students.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's why I called you here. We don't have the luxury of waiting for rescue anymore. I've decided to see whether the "boon" can be of any use.
The resigned silence conveys her feelings on the matter.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: "Boon"?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's an item Igor gave me during the Don Operation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's possible that it could generate an immunity zone. But ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But we have almost no idea what's inside it. It could save us or destroy us. It was a gift from Arcana. Let's not forget that.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Arcana?! Then, shouldn't we stay as far away from it as possible?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I think so too. It really is like Pandora's box. Once opened, there'll be no undoing the consequences.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Even so, it may be our last hope to save everyone here.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: "You are the true savior destined to lead us from the flood. Take it."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Igor believed that I was meant to have it. He was absolutely certain, though I still don't understand why.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But if I can make it work, it could shield us all from the "Storm." I'd be saving not just you two, but all the students here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Igor managed to protect his entire army from the "Flood" in Antarctica, and I believe he did it with the power of this cube.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But that's hardly for certain. What if we open it and find out there's nothing inside?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then we attempt to reach the central watchtower, assuming the Manus hasn't destroyed the Dove there too.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: They'll hit us with everything they have out there. And even if we somehow avoided them, how could we manage to get all these children out safely?
The implication leaves Merel's palms cold.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: There really aren't any options left, then.
The "boon" appears in her hands once more and casts its mysterious, unpredictable glow across the room.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I've already applied the alchemical compound Ms. Marguerite gave me. She said it will begin to dismantle the shell as soon as the incantation is recited.
Time. She needs time to calm her nerves.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Unlock   the   leaden   secret.
The momentary chaos ends, and an empty, black gate manifests ahead.
An extraordinary aura radiates out from it, painting its surroundings in colors too mystical and ancient for description.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: A gate? The "boon" is an entrance?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I hear something. A voice. Someone's calling out.
Sonetto and Merel exchange a look of suspicion.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I don't hear anything at all.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There's only wind, blowing across the ground. No voices.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's calling out to us. I hear my name and yours, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, it's entirely possible that this is a trap. Stepping in there could be exactly what Arcana wants.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But the voice ... It sounds just like mine.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Sorry, you're saying the voice coming from that gate is yours, and only you can hear it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I know how impossible it must sound.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But I want to see for myself. I have to try.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then, please, at least allow me to accompany you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Of course. Merel, can I ask you to wait here? Someone has to look after the students if we don't make it back.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You have to get them to the central tower before the library is exposed to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I-I have another idea.
Merel lifts a trembling hand. It feels as if she's back in school again, but volunteering ... That is a new sensation.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'll go to the central tower myself and bring back the Dove installed there.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: On your own? That's far too risky. The Manus are everywhere. They've likely taken control of the entire campus.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Just listen. The Manus we've encountered so far have been manageable. Tough but dumb. They haven't sent anything I can't handle.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Acting alone might even be an advantage. I'll be much quicker and quieter without trying to move all these kids with me too.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: If I shapeshift on the way, I might even be able to draw some enemies away from the library.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, go on. Check what's behind the gate. I'll head for the Dove. It probably won't last long off its pedestal, but what's left inside should be enough to get us through the "Storm."

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And if the Dove runs out of energy before the "Storm" arrives? Or what if something happens to you on the way? The stakes are too high. We can't afford to leave this to chance.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: We're already betting on luck, aren't we? And just waiting isn't going to improve our odds any more. What if you come back empty-handed? What then?
The chaos in her mind causes the words to come out knotted and unfocused.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No, we need to stack the cards, or-or spread the risk or something like that! Do you see what I mean?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: And to be honest, if you don't make it back, I doubt I could get everyone to safety by myself.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: But going out alone? That I can do. This way, we double their chances of survival.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: "Always have a plan to fall back on." Creius is always saying that to me.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: And this time, I've got one.
She punctuates her speech with a deep gasp of breath.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I admire your courage, Merel. Truly.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Go then. I trust you. And I need you to trust me, too.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We meet here again before the "Storm." And whatever happens, we move forward together.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Mhm. I promise.
Having agreed upon a rendezvous location, they exchange a final glance—a moment of utmost trust.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's time. Let's go, Sonetto.
The dark entrance welcomes them in.
A strange rumbling follows. Then, both gate and cube vanish altogether.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: They're gone.
A moment later, Lavender bursts into the study room.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Merel? What's going on? Where did Ms. Vertin and Ms. Sonetto go?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: They've gone to find a way to get us all through the "Storm" safely.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I ... I'm going to leave soon, too, Lavender. I need to get to the central watchtower and see if I can find something that might help us there.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: By yourself?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Y-Yeah. Don't worry. I know a way to slip past the enemies outside.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: Those Manus monsters have just been hanging around so far. They don't seem to be trying to get in. But even if a few try, the senior students and I should be able to manage.

items.speaker: Lavender
items.text: We'll be alright here, as long as they don't all come charging in at once. You go ahead.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I couldn't ask for more. I'll be back as soon as I can.
Lavender takes a deep breath and offers a solemn nod.
Ten seconds pass. Then, a little blackbird clumsily flies from the library's north-facing window.
